newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BCN moves into retail banking.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BCN moves into retail banking.

text.p: Brazilian private bank BCN said it will strenghten its retail banking business by launching a new product aimed at increasing its client base by about 70 percent by year's end.
BCN said its so-called "Relationship Account" will offer clients reduced banking fees, up to 18 days of interest-free credit for overdrafts and capitalization bonds to participate in lotteries.

Antonio Carlos Canto Porto Filho, executive vice-president for Products at BCN, told reporters the new product is part of the bank's strategy to end the year with about 420,000 customers. The bank now has 242,000 clients.
"We plan to grow by moving into retail, but more selectively," Porto Filho said.
BCN's move into retail banking follows the bank's decision early this year to end talks with Banco BBA Creditanstalt, which was interested in acquiring a controlling stake in the bank.
"BCN has ruled out any possibility of change in ownership and defined a new strategy for growth," said Antonio Grisi Filho, executive director vice-president.

The bank is following a trend in Brazilian banking as financial institutions, from local bank Banco Excel Economico to foreign-owned BankBoston Brazil, increasingly move to expand their retail banking business.
With the "Relationship Account", BCN clients will gain the most benefits as they strenghten their relationships with the bank by increasing deposits or acquiring insurance plans, BCN officials said.

The new product also is part of BCN's plan to focus on three segments -- individual and corporate clients with annual revenues up to $5 million; companies with revenues between $5 million and $100 million; and firms with over $100 million in revenues.
"We found that we needed to become more specialized to better serve each client," Porto Filho said.
He also said the bank's growth plans may include the opening of branches in Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro states, but no decision has been taken yet. The bank has 203 branches.
BCN is Brazil's sixth largest private bank in terms of net worth. Last year, it posted a net profit of 144.8 million reais, for a 15.5 percent annual return on equity.
The bank ended 1996 with total assets of 7.3 billion reais and a net worth of 934.8 million reais.
BCN last year acquired local bank Banco Itamarati, which was owned by former soy baron Olacyr de Moraes.
